newsitem.title: USA: NASD Regulation has advertising investigation unit.
newsitem.headline: NASD Regulation has advertising investigation unit.

text.p: NASD Regulation, the securities industry regulator, on Monday said it has formed a new panel to investigate complaints from consumers and others about the advertisements and marketing materials firms distribute.

"The tremendous growth in the volume and the variety of sales materials disseminated in the securities industry today demand that NASD Regulation move aggressively to ensure investors are protected," said R. Clark Hooper, Senior Vice President of disclosure and investor protection.
She said in addition to focussing more resources, NASD Regulation thought it important to create this new unit to help coordinate investigations.

Amy Sochard, a long-time NASD Regulation official, will head the new unit. She has been working in NASD Regulation's advertising regulation department since 1986. That department reviews all advertising and sales materials used by the more than 5,500 broker-dealer firms.
Officials there said the advertising regulation department will also increase its random checks of marketing materials.
"These steps are all focused on ensuring that investors receive information that's accurate, timely, and helpful," said Thomas M. Selman, director of the advertising regulation department.
